# slates_native

Generated by `conformance/vectors/src/slates/native.rs`. `lepic.v1`, the native slate layout of the
EPICTX specification (section 5.10), has no upstream implementation: the generator encodes it from
the specification alone, reading the V3 JSON `epic-wallet` wrote for the same slate, and calls no
LEPIC code. `upstream` names the wallet whose flows produced the slates; the flows are the ones of
the `slates` area, run once and shared, so slate ids and keys match `../slates`. Regenerate with
`cargo xtask vectors generate --area slates_native`; the area is deterministic. Envelope and
encoding rules are in `../README.md`.

## Slates

`<case>_<stage>_<network>.json`: every stage of every `slates` flow, once for mainnet and once for
floonet. The test chain's slates sit below both networks' first hard fork. The `_after_fork`
variants move the height and TTL cutoff past it by `inputs.height_shift`, so they carry block header
version 7.

| `inputs` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `case`, `stage` | The `slates` flow and stage the slate comes from. |
| `network` | The network byte the slate was encoded for. |
| `base` | The `slates` vector of the same slate in V3 JSON. |
| `height_shift` | Present on `_after_fork` cases: the blocks added to the height and TTL cutoff. |
| `tail` | The TLV tail records appended after the body: `reply_key`, `reply_mailbox` and `unknown` records. Flow slates have none. |
| `v3_json` | The V3 JSON the slate was encoded from, after any height shift. |

| `expected` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `size` | The length of `lepic_v1` in bytes. |
| `lepic_v1` | The encoded slate, hex. |
| `view` | The slate's JSON view. |

A reader decodes `lepic_v1` for `network`, checks it decodes to the same slate as `v3_json`, encodes
it back to the same bytes, and compares its view with `view`.

## Slates with a tail

`tail_<label>_<case>_<stage>_mainnet.json`: a flow slate with a TLV tail. `unknown` adds ignorable
records of unknown types, which a decoder keeps as they are, to an S1 and an S3; `reply_key` and
`reply_mailbox` give a raw S1 a reply key, and a reply key and mailbox; `reply_mailbox_unknown`
gives a raw I1 both and an unknown record. Fields are those of the slates above.

## Malformed slates

`malformed_<name>.json`: a flow slate changed so that a decoder must refuse it.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inputs.base` | The vector in this area the bytes start from. |
| `inputs.mutation` | What was changed. |
| `inputs.decode_network` | The network the bytes are decoded for. |
| `inputs.lepic_v1` | The refused bytes, hex. |
| `expected.error` | The refusal: a variant of LEPIC's `NativeError`, or `Tail.<variant>` and `Model.<variant>` for a refused tail record and a refused slate model. |
